evidence.description: The `state` computed property performs a sort operation on every access, which can be inefficient if the `items` set is large.

candidates.explanation: Performing sorting inside a computed property means the O(n log n) operation is executed every time the property is accessed, rather than being cached or performed only when the underlying data changes.
candidates.title: Inefficient Computed Property

evidence.description: The `decoder` property is recalculated every time it is accessed.

candidates.explanation: The `decoder` property creates a new `JSONDecoder` instance and configures it every time it is accessed, which is inefficient. It should be stored as a private constant or lazy property.
candidates.title: Inefficient Property Calculation

evidence.description: The `items` property triggers a `DispatchQueue.main.async` block that maps the `state` and calls `send`, but the `state` property itself is a computed property that performs a sort.
The `state` property is used within the `didSet` of `items`.

candidates.explanation: Calling `self?.state.map` inside a `didSet` that is triggered by an assignment to `items` creates a complex flow where a computed property's logic (sorting) is executed during a side-effect on the main thread.
candidates.title: Complex Side-Effect in Property Observer

evidence.description: The `needsUpdate` property accesses `User.shared.news` and `Calendar.current` directly, creating a dependency on a global shared instance.

candidates.explanation: Accessing `User.shared` inside a property makes the class harder to test and tightly couples the `News` class to a specific singleton instance.
candidates.title: Tight Coupling to Singleton

evidence.description: The `save` method uses a `do-catch` block that suppresses all errors.

candidates.explanation: Swallowing errors in a `do-catch` block without logging or handling them makes it difficult to diagnose failures in data persistence (e.g., disk full, permission issues).
candidates.title: Swallowed Exceptions
